title: Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council deputy minister says Chinese cyberattacks occur almost daily ahead of local elections
date_note: Focus Taiwan (27 November) says he spoke at the council's regular press briefing on 26 November.
summary: Focus Taiwan (CNA, Japanese) reports that Mainland Affairs Council deputy minister Liang Wen-chieh said cyberattacks from China occur almost every day ahead of Taiwan's local elections on 28 November. He cited National Security Bureau data of 2.58 million intrusions or disruptions per day. He called on the Ministry of Digital Affairs and election commissions to keep vote-counting systems running normally.
plain: Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council says, as reported by Focus Taiwan, that cyberattacks from China happen almost daily before the local elections, at 2.58 million per day by National Security Bureau data.
exec: A Taiwanese official says attacks from China are almost daily before the local elections, citing 2.58 million per day; he urged vote-counting systems to keep running normally.

validation.note: Only Focus Taiwan (CNA) was read; the council's own transcript was not read.

review.note: Compared date 26 Nov, 2.58 million/day NSB figure, elections 28 Nov and statements against Focus Taiwan
